claim.quote: yielding an upper limit on the branching ratio of B($\mu^+\to e^+\gamma$) < $7.5 \times 10^{-13}$ (90% C.L.). The combination of this result and the limit obtained by MEG gives B($\mu^+\to e^+\gamma$) < $3.1 \times 10^{-13}$ (90% C.L.), which is the most stringent limit to date.

name: A search for μ⁺ → e⁺γ with the first dataset of the MEG II experiment

significance.quote: yielding an upper limit on the branching ratio of B($\mu^+\to e^+\gamma$) < $7.5 \times 10^{-13}$ (90% C.L.)

summary.plain: MEG II searched for the very rare muon decay μ⁺ → e⁺γ in its first physics run (2021) and saw no excess over the expected background: B < 7.5×10⁻¹³ (90% C.L.). Combined with the earlier MEG limit, B < 3.1×10⁻¹³, which the paper calls the most stringent limit to date.
summary.technical: Result from the first MEG II physics run (2021): no excess of events over the expected background, B(μ⁺→e⁺γ) < 7.5×10⁻¹³ (90% C.L.), with a median expected limit (sensitivity) of 8.8×10⁻¹³; combined with the limit obtained by MEG, B < 3.1×10⁻¹³ (90% C.L.), which the paper calls the most stringent limit to date. A ten-fold larger sample was being collected in 2022-2023 at the time of the paper.

title: A search for mu+ -> e+ gamma with the first dataset of the MEG II experiment
why_it_matters: MEG II is an upgrade of the MEG experiment that aims to improve the sensitivity to the μ⁺→e⁺γ branching ratio by one order of magnitude within the next few years (the paper's introduction); this is its first result.
